<subagent sessionID="ses_e4d44ddecffe2DHCVxAb5BD3WX" state="completed">
These are safe, high-impact visual-only improvements grounded in the current code and all fit the existing Canvas 2D pipeline without changing game rules or data:

- /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/renderer.js — `render()` and `drawTile()`
  - Add a stronger tile-edge separation pass: darker contour lines on shore/water/path boundaries, plus a subtle shadow under each diamond tile. The code already does neighborhood checks (`waterAlong`, region accents, grass tufts), so this would be a cheap readability boost with no gameplay impact.
  - Increase depth readability by slightly varying the land tile brightness based on world position and camera angle, rather than only palette/variant noise. Right now the map is attractive but can flatten at a distance; a small back-to-front shade ramp would keep the isometric floor legible.

- /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/renderer.js — `buildGround()` and `render()`
  - Use a subtle “ground shadow” or soft overlay under entities and props before the world is drawn, rather than relying only on the object pixels. This would preserve the crisp pixel look while making silhouettes read faster, especially against water, mist, and darker regions.
  - Add a region-specific atmospheric layer: more pronounced haze for `mistgrave`, slightly warmer bloom for `sunscorch`, cooler blue haze for `frostpeak`. Existing palette-driven logic and fog layers already show the hook; this would be a visual-only polish step.

- /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/renderer.js — `drawWeather()`
  - Slightly vary particle size and opacity by region/weather type with a more layered pass (e.g., leaves and spores with a second, softer blur-like layer). The weather system is already tuned to each kind, so a second pass would feel richer without altering logic.
  - Keep the particles in screen space but add a small “wind drift” tint and jitter to match world direction. This makes weather feel more anchored to the environment instead of flat, uniform motion.

- /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/sprites.js — `drawCharacter()`
  - Add a consistent 1-pixel outline or darker silhouette behind each body part before fill. The sprite logic already uses `shade()` heavily; an outline pass would improve readability in dense scenes and combat, especially for armor and hair colors close to the background.
  - Increase contrast on the head/helmet boundary and on limb joints. This is a very safe improvement because it would only enhance readability, not change shape composition.

- /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/sprites.js — `drawHair()`, `drawHelmet()`, and `drawArmsAndWeapon()`
  - Add a more deliberate highlight pass for rare gear and hair using the existing rarity colors (`RARITIES[...]` and `EQUIP_COLOR`). This would make high-tier gear more legible and more visually distinct without affecting gameplay.
  - For classes that already have strong silhouette cues (warrior armor, mage robe, archer bow), use a tiny rim highlight on the main torso or weapon edge. It would add polish while preserving the low-res style.

- /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/sprites.js — `drawEnemy()`
  - Give each enemy kind a stronger ground shadow and a clearer eye/face accent. The switch cases already define silhouettes; adding a base shadow ellipse and slightly stronger eye contrast would make enemies read better against foliage and shadows.
  - Increase hit-flash and state contrast slightly (chase/idle/attack) using the existing `hitFlash` and `attackAnim` logic. This would preserve the same animation data but make combat feedback clearer.

- /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/sprites.js — `drawMount()` and `drawPet()`
  - Add a soft shadow ellipse under mounts and pets and slightly adjust idle bob amplitude. The code already animates bob and gait, so this is a classic visual-only improvement with almost no risk.
  - Increase the pet’s aura or “glow” in the same aesthetic style as the character aura system. It would read better in motion and on darker backgrounds without changing pet behavior.

- /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/sprites.js — `drawWings()`
  - Add a subtle contour to the wing membranes and feather layers, with slightly more layering between foreground and background wings. Since wings are already drawn in stacked pixel layers, this would be a straightforward, low-risk depth pass.

If you want the best ROI with lowest risk, the first three are the strongest:
1) tile-edge contrast + shadow in `renderer.js`
2) outline/silhouette contrast for characters and enemies in `sprites.js`
3) rarity glow/highlight pass on gear and wings

These are all visual-only tweaks that align with the current art direction and existing functions.
